---
title: "Compare groups with facets"
---

Split a scatterplot of car weight against fuel economy into one panel for each number of cylinders.

## Data

`Datasets::mtcars()` returns the 32 cars of R's `mtcars` data, bundled with phiz as [`resources/data/mtcars.csv`](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz/blob/main/resources/data/mtcars.csv). The example uses three of its columns:

| model | mpg | cyl | wt |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mazda RX4 | 21.0 | 6 | 2.620 |
| Mazda RX4 Wag | 21.0 | 6 | 2.875 |
| Datsun 710 | 22.8 | 4 | 2.320 |

`wt` is the weight in thousands of pounds, `mpg` is the fuel economy in miles per gallon, and `cyl` is the number of cylinders.

## Code

{{< include ../_generated/example-facets-code.md >}}

Runnable script: [`facets.php`](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz/blob/main/docs/examples/scripts/facets.php) (PHP 8.5+) or [`facets.chain.php`](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz/blob/main/docs/examples/scripts/facets.chain.php) (PHP 8.3–8.4).

## Result

{{< include ../_generated/example-facets-output.md >}}

- **Shared scales.** By default every panel has the same axis ranges, so positions compare across panels.
- **Free scales.** `scales: 'free'`, `'free_x'`, or `'free_y'` gives each panel its own ranges. Positions then no longer compare across panels.
- **Mixed effects.** Heavier cars also tend to have more cylinders. Each panel shows the weight and economy association among cars with the same cylinder count.
- **Small groups.** The panels hold 11, 7, and 14 cars, so a trend within one panel is a rough description.

In R: `ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~cyl, ncol = 3)`.
